checks: Compared the full raw files byte for byte. The only difference is one dollar sign added to close the p(R) display. The display is correctly paired, all other statement text matches, and the proof and all metadata are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Verified that the proof still invokes the fixed-sector minimum, and that its statement and the quadrilateral use the same p(R). The unchanged conclusion provides one incident core at each target node for this feasible minimum at fixed positive W. The dependency record now binds the corrected exact candidate.

At a minimum one core edge meets each of nodes 1 and 4 by the same-batch fixed-area theorem; exactly two cores then forces the four stated pairs, and their endpoints are disjoint. The canonical determinants are one, so exactly the two core entries vanish and the other four off-diagonal edge entries are strictly negative.

Enumerated all components: (0,3) gives (1,2,3) and (4,5,0); (0,4) gives (1,2,3,4) and (5,0); (1,3) gives (2,3) and (4,5,0,1); (1,4) gives (2,3,4) and (5,0,1). Both target nodes are endpoints of their respective paths, possibly in the same path. The only two-node paths have no target node.

For a positive definite path of at least three nodes, an internal radius is outside the target chord and incident to two noncore edges. Decreasing it slightly keeps the exact core products, improves its adjacent product constraints, and changes only the selected block, which remains positive definite by continuity. The target chord stays fixed and exactly one other chord decreases, strictly decreasing p.

For the two-node path, either chosen radius is non-target, and its unique incident core edge leads to a target node in the other path. Replacing the selected radius R by R−δ and multiplying that target radius by R/(R−δ) keeps the crossing core product exactly fixed. The other core endpoints are disjoint, and all four strictly noncore products retain slack for sufficiently small δ.

In the last perturbation the decreased-radius block stays positive definite by continuity. The increased-radius block changes only a diagonal and an incident internal edge pair, both entrywise increasing, with nonpositive off-diagonals. Its PSD follows by comparing quadratic forms on |x|. The off-block core entries stay zero. By the exact criterion the perturbed vector is actually realized; the target chord grows and one other chord shrinks, both improving p strictly.

Both PSD blocks are singular after exclusion of positive definiteness. A nonzero kernel vector can be replaced by its absolute value without raising its form; PSD then makes that vector a null vector. A zero coordinate forces its adjacent coordinates to vanish because the internal off-diagonals are strictly negative. Connectivity makes the null vector strictly positive. Concatenating and using the same-batch rigidity theorem gives exactly four strict open-sector vertices and uniqueness of the body.
